messages:
samir: Hey team — starting intake for nebula-7b (community fork). Found model card + weights here: https://models.example/nebula-7b and weights tarball link. Quick license/usage check before we add to internal catalog or run quant experiments. :eyes:

maya: Thx. Quick scan — model card mentions 'research use only' and a link to the license PDF. Can you paste the exact license header?

samir: Pasted from weights repo README:
```
SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0
This model and weights are provided under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0.
```

oliver: If it's CC-BY-NC-SA, that NC bit usually blocks commercial hosting. Does our hosted API count as commercial?

legal-bot: Preliminary: CC-BY-NC-SA prohibits use 'primarily intended for or directed toward commercial advantage or monetary compensation.' Offering it via our hosted pay-as-you-go API is likely commercial. Private/dedicated contractual deployments might be allowed if the customer is noncommercial, but commercial customers would be a problem. Recommend full legal review. :warning:

tess: Also note SA (ShareAlike) can create derivative distribution obligations if we redistribute modified weights (e.g., quantized). Need to know if quantization counts as a derivative under that license.

samir: Good point. Our quantization pipeline produces new weight files and we sometimes ship quantized weights to Dedicated customers. That could be redistribution.

infra-bot: license-checker: scanned repo, flags: ["NC clause", "SA clause", "no commercial exception noted"]. Report: https://internal/reports/license/nebula-7b/1860001111

maya: For immediate action, I'd propose we: 1) Hold adding nebula-7b to hosted catalog; 2) Allow internal evals (air-gapped) for benchmark comparisons under research use; 3) Block quantized weights distribution until legal clears. Thoughts?

oliver: Agree. Can we do benchmarking with inference-only skeleton (no weight export) — like run evals inside a restricted environment and only export metrics?

samir: Yep, we can run evals on an isolated infra pool and only extract metrics. No weight artifacts leave the isolation.

legal-bot: Action: open a legal intake ticket, tag licensing team, and include the links + our intended usage patterns (hosted API, dedicated redistribution, private deploys). Expected turnaround 3–5 business days.

tess: I'll open the ticket. Also propose a temporary label on the model in our intake tracker: `license:hold-nc-sa` and a risk note.

samir: Cool. Also noting product ask: some customers requested nebula-7b for low-cost inference — they'll likely push for dedicated hosting. We'll need a legal decision before sales conversations continue.

maya: Capture checklist for this thread so we don't forget during onboarding:
- [ ] Confirm SPDX/license header (done)
- [ ] Run automated license scanner (infra-bot done)
- [ ] Legal intake + review (tess -> opened)
- [ ] Decide allowed deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
- [ ] Determine whether quantization/weight redistribution allowed
- [ ] If allowed, create footprint policy for quantized artifact distribution

samir: Assigned: tess -> open ticket, oliver -> set up isolated eval pool and run perf/quality baselines, maya -> pause any catalog work, me -> notify customer contacts.

tess: Ticket opened: LIC-2026-334 (link: https://tickets.internal/LIC-2026-334). Assigned to licensing@redwood. I added context and infra report.

oliver: Will schedule isolated evals tomorrow, will post results in this thread as soon as available.

maya: Thanks. For tracking, I'm adding `license:hold` tag to model intake entry.

samir: OK leaving this on hold until legal responds. Marking status: HOLD. :thumbsup:

legal-bot: Note: if licensing team approves commercial hosting under a separate commercial license or contributor exception, we will update intake with specific permitted deployment modes and redistribution rules.

maya: Great — follow-up once LIC-2026-334 resolves.

samir: Thanks all.
